title: Tightness of x-only interpolation degree bounds
question: Tightness conjecture for x-only interpolation: for E/F_p, P of prime order r and 2N < r, every g in F_p[X] with g(x(kP)) = k (resp. k^2) for 1 <= k <= N has deg g >= N − c for an absolute constant c (generic curves), improving the proven bound (N − 2)/3; or else there exist families with substantially lower-degree interpolants.
rationale: Derived by PI from the observed gap (proven ~N/3, observed N−1) in ECDLP-25/26 toy data.
claims: Tightness conjecture for x-only interpolation: for E/F_p, P of prime order r and 2N < r, every g in F_p[X] with g(x(kP)) = k (resp. k^2) for 1 <= k <= N has deg g >= N − c for an absolute constant c (generic curves), improving the proven bound (N − 2)/3; or else there exist families with substantially lower-degree interpolants.
next_action: New technique needed (e.g. using the divided-difference/Newton structure or algebraic relations among the nodes).
notes: PI-derived follow-up from proven theorems. | ECDLP-33: gap not closed; L2 shows the translation-annihilator method cannot beat N/3 (HYP-0d4f14da-d669-43e4-9ba2-2d83a5cdb75c); experiments support N−1−O(1) generically (HYP-a8d1f541-ea3a-4804-8ee2-064de21d06d3); structured CM family with constant deficit (L3).
